references.phrase: integrability of real random variable X and Z
references.context: Probability theory: integrable real random variable X on a probability space with E[|X|]<∞, equivalently ∫|X|dP finite; applies separately to X and Z.
references.matching_note: Source-free provisional target candidate; review cross-formulation equivalence and distinct foundational probability/topology/algebra scope later.
Z is a real-valued random variable using the sub-sigma-algebra G as its domain measurability structure; reuse existing real random-variable definition with that G.

references.disposition: Equality of restricted integrals ∫_A Z dP=∫_A X dP for every A∈G is the defining characterization of a conditional expectation version, not a previously assumed expectation.
It is determined only up to almost-sure equality; an arbitrary representative satisfying both conditions counts.
